evidence.paraphrase: Toby describes the seaplane's technical performance specifications: a thousand-mile radius and ceiling above twenty thousand feet.
evidence.quote: She\u2019s worth looking at, too--built for a radius of a thousand miles and a ceiling of over twenty thousand feet.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains the machine's original design as a super-fighting-scout with large radius and climbing capacity.
evidence.quote: She was, as he explained to me, intended for a super-fighting-scout, with an immense radius, a great capacity for climb, and a second machine-gun.

evidence.paraphrase: Toby questions whether empty space truly contains nothing between here and the stars.
evidence.quote: There can\u2019t be nothingness all the way, can there?\u201d he demanded of me with a curious vehemence of interrogation.

evidence.paraphrase: Toby contrasts the accepted astronomical view of empty space with his belief that something lies hidden in the blue distance.
evidence.quote: At a distance everything melts into the blue. I have seen blank blue sky where on another day there\u2019s a range of mountains sharp and clear across the horizon. And they pretend that in all those millions of miles there is nothing--nothing but empty space!

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes his loss of nerve for flying after his last wartime flight.
evidence.quote: I had landed by a miracle with my nerve suddenly gone. I had never been in the air since--for a long time could not look at an airplane without a fit of trembling.

evidence.paraphrase: Toby speculates that continuing to climb higher would lead to reaching some other place.
evidence.quote: didn\u2019t you ever feel that if you went a little higher--climbed and climbed--you would come to something--some other place? Didn\u2019t it almost seem to you that it would be as easy as going back?

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator recalls the traumatic wartime moment that broke his nerve and makes flying nauseating.
evidence.quote: the mere idea of going up in that machine made me feel sick inside, still so powerful was the memory of that moment long ago when, ten thousand feet up with a Hun just below me plunging in flames to destruction, I had felt my nerve suddenly break, my head go dizzy in an awful panic.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts with fear and trembling during the ascent.
evidence.quote: I sank back into my seat, quivering.

evidence.paraphrase: At extreme altitude the passengers suffer physiological effects and would soon require oxygen.
evidence.quote: We must have been somewhere about twenty thousand feet. My head seemed as though it would burst. I was breathing with difficulty. A little higher, and we should need oxygen.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes the physical effects of high altitude: cold, dizziness, blood-pressure changes, and labored breathing.
evidence.quote: Thirteen thousand--thirteen thousand five hundred--fourteen thousand--fourteen thousand five hundred--fifteen thousand--I gave it up. It was icily cold. My head was dizzy, my ears sizzling with altered blood-pressure. My lungs heaved in this rarefied atmosphere.

evidence.paraphrase: Toby declares his intention to keep flying upward with Sylvia rather than returning.
Toby intends to keep climbing indefinitely upward toward some destination.
evidence.quote: Up there! On and on, until we come to--

evidence.paraphrase: Toby speaks of a way beyond the stars as a real destination he is seeking.
evidence.quote: You think you know the way beyond the stars?

evidence.paraphrase: Toby, apparently deranged, fires a pistol at the narrator in mid-flight.
evidence.quote: he was leveling that automatic pistol at me. I could see by his eyes that he was in the very act of pressing the trigger for the second time.

evidence.paraphrase: The airplane plunges into a dangerous vertical spin during the struggle.
evidence.quote: We were vertically nose down, spinning horribly

evidence.paraphrase: After recovering the plane, the narrator finds Toby has fallen out and is gone.
evidence.quote: only when I pulled her out of it, circled her round once for a long steady glide, did I realize that I was alone in that cockpit. There was no Toby!

evidence.paraphrase: In the crisis the narrator's nerve returns and his panic disappears.
evidence.quote: Curiously enough, in that moment of crisis, I found my head as clear, my nerves as steady, as they had ever been in my life. All my dizzy turmoil had vanished. I forgot that I had ever had a panic in the air.

evidence.paraphrase: Descending through the clouds, the narrator glimpses the sea and a distant steamship far below.
evidence.quote: I saw a deep black gulf riven in its snowy mass--saw down through that gulf a tiny model steamship trailing a long white wake....
